summary: All five round-2 findings are closed, and I re-ran the mutation battery myself rather than accepting the reported numbers. Baseline 36 passed in migration.test.ts, 84 across 6 files; tsc --noEmit and npm run build both exit 0. The two author-claimed kills reproduce exactly: returning the exported GROUP_IDS reference from the non-array branch → 2 fail (`groupOrder null → default order`, `two boards with a null groupOrder…`), and an in-place-mutating sanitizer → 2 fail (`duplicate collapsed`, `already valid and non-default`). I also probed the harder version of major #2 that the author did not claim: a module-level shared array that is NOT GROUP_IDS itself — the sort of regression a well-meaning 'avoid re-allocating' refactor introduces — and it dies too, on both the same tests. That makes the pair of assertions non-redundant: `not.toBe(GROUP_IDS)` catches handing out the constant, `not.toBe(sanitizeGroupOrder(undefined))` catches handing out any shared instance, and the new v8 two-board test pins it end-to-end on the path the v7 test provably cannot reach. The renamed missing-group test is now honest and load-bearing in both directions: a GROUP_IDS loop in the sanitization block still kills it, and so does the opposite mutant — making migrateData recreate the absent group kills it via the new `groups.orgIntentions` residual assertion. So the test pins 'not recreated' as the tested contract rather than merely failing to notice it. Every round-1 kill survives re-verification: sanitization restricted to boards[0] → 2 fail (up from 1, the new test adds a kill), surrogate guard removed → 1, freshDefaultData's explicit array copy removed → 2. I extended the battery well past the prior rounds — 18 mutants in total across both sanitizers and the migration ladder — and found no further survivor that this task owns: dropping the duplicate check → 3 fail, the unknown-id check → 4, the missing-ids append loop → 7, sanitizing groupOrder only when undefined → 6, removing the title-sanitization block → 2, removing trim → 5, an off-by-one cap → 4, trim-after-slice → 3, coercing non-strings → 1. The decisions log was absent when I first checked and present when I checked again: the Task 03 section now carries the (a)/(b)/(c) content verbatim as specified, both pre-authorised out-of-scope observations, and the Task 07 cross-task consequence stated as a contract rather than buried. Nothing blocks completion. The one deliberate survivor is unchanged and correctly recorded: reducing the `version < 8` block to `result.version = 8` still leaves 36 green, because the unconditional sanitization block overwrites both fields — task step 5 mandates the block shape, so the code is right to keep it and the log says so plainly. The three findings below are all carry-forward; none is actionable inside this task's scope and I would not hold the task for any of them.

findings.location: src/data/migration.ts:154-159 (sanitization block) — carry to Task 07 or a later hardening task
findings.issue: The suite pins that a board missing one GROUP entry does not throw, but a board missing the whole `groups` object still does. I verified it directly: with `delete board.groups` on an otherwise valid v8 file, migrateData throws `TypeError: Cannot convert undefined or null to object` from `Object.values(board.groups)`, and since migrateData runs before the first render this is the exact failure mode the missing-group test exists to prevent — the user gets no board at all. This is a strictly rarer hand-edit than a missing group key and it belongs to the same class as the missing/non-array `result.boards` guard that the task's implementation hints explicitly decline (on the sound grounds that `cleanupCompletedTasks` in main.ts dies on the same data two lines later). Recording it because the decisions log documents the `result.boards` decision but not this neighbouring one, so the boundary of what 'does not throw on hand-edited data' actually guarantees is currently narrower than a reader of the log would infer.
findings.recommendation: Do not add a guard in Task 03 — that is the hardening the hints forbid, and a guard here without one on `result.boards` would be arbitrary. Extend the existing decisions-log bullet about `result.boards` to name this case too, so the guarantee is scoped honestly: 'a missing group key is survived; a missing groups object is not, and is out of scope for the same reason as result.boards'. If a later task does take on load-time hardening, the test is one line beside the existing missing-group test: build the same v8 input, `delete data.boards[0].groups`, and assert `expect(() => migrateData(data)).not.toThrow()` — which fails on today's code, so it must land with the fix, not before it. No mock changes; pure function on plain data.

findings.location: src/data/migration.ts:137-159 — carry-forward, matches the tech-debt note already in the decisions log
findings.issue: The forward-compatibility path the decisions log flags as tech debt has no test. I ran it: a file with `version: 9` skips every migration block but still enters the unconditional sanitization block, so an unknown id in groupOrder is silently dropped, a title on an unknown group is capped to 40, `result.version` stays 9, and the whole thing is written straight back to data.json by loadPluginData(). That is exactly the 'old build opens a newer synced vault' scenario the log describes. Blast radius today is genuinely zero — no schema above 8 exists — so this is documentation-of-intent rather than a defect, and I flag it only because the behaviour is currently asserted nowhere: any future change to the sanitization block's placement would alter it without a single test noticing.
findings.recommendation: Not for this task. When schema 9 is introduced (or the group set changes), add one test alongside the existing `groupOrder is sanitized on already-migrated v8 data`: feed `{ version: 9, boards: [board with groupOrder ['completed','archive'] ] }`, then assert `result.version === 9` (the file is not downgraded) and whatever the then-current decision is about unknown ids — either `toEqual` the sanitized permutation if silent dropping is accepted, or that unknown ids survive if forward-compat wins. Pinning the choice at that point is what makes the log's tech-debt note actionable. No mock changes.

findings.location: tests/unit/migration.test.ts:298 (`a board missing a group does not throw (the missing group is not recreated)`)
findings.issue: `expect(result.boards[0].groupOrder).toContain('orgIntentions')` is fully implied by the `toEqual` three lines above it, which already asserts the complete six-element array including 'orgIntentions'. I could not construct any mutant that the toContain kills and the toEqual does not. Purely cosmetic: it costs one line and no runtime, and it is arguably earning its place as documentation — it sits directly beside the `toBeUndefined` assertion and the two together are what make the residual readable as 'the id is in the order, the group is not in groups'. Flagging it for completeness rather than because it should change.
findings.recommendation: Leave it. If a future edit touches this test anyway, the redundancy can be removed by folding the intent into the comment rather than the assertion — but removing it now would trade a readable pairing for nothing, and re-verifying the test after a cosmetic edit costs more than the line does. Explicitly not a reason to hold the task.
